ca_360_degree_boulder.blurb: A lone sandstone block of roughly ten feet, tucked among trees a short stroll downhill from the main Castle Rock formation. It holds about a dozen boulder problems: two or three easy ones at V0 and V1, a solid middle of V2 to V4 lines, and a single V8 that circles the entire block. Canopy shade keeps it cool and the walls are short, though a pad is worth having for the topouts. It makes a relaxed, low-commitment stop for climbers working through the larger Castle Rock bouldering circuit rather than a destination on its own.

ca_3_east_face_main.blurb: The biggest wall on the east side of the Snowshed cliff at Donner Pass, just off the I-80 corridor near Lake Tahoe. Twelve granodiorite lines mix eight trad routes, many of them cracks, with four sport lines. Difficulty leans hard: most routes sit at 5.11, three are 5.13 and one is 5.14, with a lone 5.9 and 5.10 for warming up. The face drops into shade around midday, which makes it a pleasant pick for a hot summer evening. Walls here are vertical and up to about eighty feet.

ca_foothill_crag_the_foot.blurb: A small, gritty sandstone cliff on the north side of a hill just outside Ojai, with a quiet, forested feel and a cooler north-facing exposure. A dozen routes mix trad, bolted lines and one top-rope, from a walk-up grade through 5.8 and 5.9 to a handful at 5.10 and one 5.11. Bolts are spread out, so a small rack of cams adds comfort, and every line can be top-roped from fixed or natural anchors with some extra webbing. Expect a half-hour walk in and little company.
ca_foothill_crag_the_foot.parking_note: Leave the car at the small trailhead lot off Signal Street, at the edge of town, and walk from there.
ca_foothill_crag_the_foot.approach: From the lot, follow the path between the houses to Foothill Road, pass through the gate and continue up the dirt road. A trail forks off to the right and leads to the base of the cliff, which sits on the north side of the hill.

ca_mini_buttress_3.blurb: A compact sport wall in the Big Chief area of the Truckee River Canyon, north of Lake Tahoe, set beside the Center Wall. Twelve routes, eleven bolted and one top-rope, mostly short with a couple of longer outings. The grades spread from 5.6 to 5.12, with a handful of easier 5.6 to 5.9 lines, four at 5.10 and a few at 5.11, so it suits mixed groups. The ridge it sits on is mainly a summer and fall destination, high above the canyon.
ca_mini_buttress_3.approach: Follow the Big Chief trail up to the saddle and drop through the notch, then turn left. A few minutes of walking past the towers, a cave and the Center Wall brings you to the buttress, which sits right next to that wall.

ca_low_profile_dome.blurb: A low granodiorite dome on the north side of Highway 120 in Tuolumne Meadows, roughly 8,500 feet up and close to the road, with a short, obvious walk to the base. Eleven of the twelve routes are trad, plus one bolted line, running from 5.7 up to 5.11. Most land in the 5.9 and 5.10 range, with a couple of easier moderates. Several climbs are two or three pitches, and knob climbing is a feature. The dome picks up early sun and works well on a cool morning, with views over the neighboring domes.
